trigger: Skipped skill prompts, wrote throwaway inline Plugin API code for 488 ops; correct but burned excessive tokens and bypassed tested tooling.
lesson: Always use the existing pipeline scripts (audit/resolve/bulk-update/token-lookup) — never write ad-hoc inline Plugin API code for tree walks or bulk writes.

trigger: Bound 4 corners with 4 individual setBoundVariable calls — slow.
lesson: setBoundVariable('cornerRadius', v) binds all 4 corners in one call — ~5x faster than per-corner.

trigger: Fixed setup cost per mcp_figma_use_figma call ~7.5s (getNodeByIdAsync ~1.8s + 4x parallel getVariableByIdAsync ~5.6s).
lesson: Amortise setup cost over as many nodes as possible in one use_figma call (308 nodes in one call/78s is fine). Avoid many small calls.

trigger: getLocalVariablesAsync returns 514 vars — slow.
lesson: For NV-only writes with known IDs, skip getLocalVariablesAsync; use getVariableByIdAsync via Promise.all. Cache the name→id map per fileKey+version.

trigger: figma.getLocalEffectStyles() (sync) returned empty/stale in some Plugin API contexts, giving a false ∅ in QA.
lesson: Always use the async read APIs (getLocalEffectStylesAsync, getLocalVariablesAsync). Sync style/variable reads can be stale.

trigger: Needed to bind fills on icon VECTORs inside INSTANCE children.
lesson: setBoundVariableForPaint works on nested instance-override nodes — traverse comp.children recursively; no getNodeByIdAsync per node needed.

trigger: Ordering of textStyleId vs fill on TEXT nodes.
lesson: textStyleId assignment on TEXT nodes is synchronous and works on instance-override TEXT nodes; assign before fill to avoid ordering issues.

trigger: 'The user cancelled the tool call' was misread as a Figma/network hang.
lesson: A cancelled tool call means the user clicked Cancel in the approval dialog, not a network hang. Run a 2-line smoke test to prove connectivity before bulk writes.

trigger: Sync figma.getNodeById can fail to resolve inner node IDs mid-script.
lesson: Always use figma.getNodeByIdAsync; obtain inner node refs via tree traversal, never getNodeById in a loop.

trigger: Planning a future swap from the local .hercules store to a real Hercules install.
lesson: Real Hercules contracts: state=SessionDB (~/.hercules/state.db) with a state_meta k/v table — map state.write(runId) -> set_meta('run:<runId>', json), same pattern as goal:<id>. A run=kanban_db.Run (claim->complete|blocked|failed|timeout|reclaimed). The ODIN loop=goals.py Ralph loop (status active|paused|done|cleared, judge verdict done|continue). Skills(SKILL.md, loaded on demand) vs Memory(compact, injected). manifest.json=a skill-bundle {name,description,skills[],instruction}. Keep these analogies intact.

trigger: FDS-Card audit: Padding=True uses TS key `spacing` (maps to itemSpacing/gap) instead of `verticalPadding`/`horizontalPadding`; also uses generic fds-spacing-200 instead of the component-specific fds-spacing-const-container-card.
lesson: For card/container components: check that TS uses `verticalPadding`/`horizontalPadding` keys (not `spacing`) for padding insets. Prefer fds-spacing-const-container-card over fds-spacing-200 for card internal padding.

ruleProposal.diff: # Consider adding a rule: FDS-Card Padding=True -> key verticalPadding + horizontalPadding -> spacing.fds-spacing-const.container.fds-spacing-const-container-card

trigger: COMPONENT_SET with zero GROUPs and all COMPONENT children already VERTICAL AL.
lesson: When a COMPONENT_SET scan returns zero GROUPs and all COMPONENT children have non-NONE layoutMode, classify the run property-only: emit only sizing/slot-AL property corrections, no structural OPS. Note: Figma 2025+ SLOT nodes inside a COMPONENT are writable (unlike INSTANCE internals).

trigger: FDS-Card audit: TS-only draft, wrong border token on surface theme, generic padding token.
lesson: For card/container components: (1) padding insets should use verticalPadding/horizontalPadding keys, not `spacing` (which maps to itemSpacing); prefer fds-spacing-const-container-card over generic fds-spacing-200. (2) Watch for copy-paste border-token errors across themes (surface variants carrying fds-on-alternate-surface-ulow). (3) var.fds.* TS prefix signals NV binding is intended but may be unapplied (varMap empty).

trigger: NV names searched as fds/fds-surface-variant but actual Figma names are var/fds/fds-surface-variant — file uses var/ prefix namespace.
lesson: In this Figma file (Ahvbwk0dUHeHazrQX2XtGd), all NV variable names carry a var/ prefix. Audit shorthand fds/fds-* must be looked up as var/fds/fds-* in getLocalVariablesAsync. Always verify by running a discovery pass before the write pass on a new file.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add note: this file's NV names use var/ prefix (e.g. var/fds/fds-surface-variant, not fds/fds-surface-variant). Verify with discovery pass before write pass.

trigger: bulk-update.figma.js nv-type uses setBoundVariable(prop,v) which does not work for fills/strokes (paint arrays require setBoundVariableForPaint). Also has no ts-strip type.
lesson: bulk-update.figma.js nv-type is scalar-props-only (cornerRadius, strokeWeight, padding…). For fills/strokes NV binding use a targeted script with setBoundVariableForPaint. For TS key removal, setSharedPluginData(ns, key, '') strips the key. Document this gap in the script header.

trigger: Audit shorthand fds/fds-* did not match the actual Figma variable names, which carry a var/ prefix (var/fds/fds-*). First write on a new file failed to resolve until a getLocalVariablesAsync discovery pass.
lesson: On the FIRST NV write to any new fileKey, run a getLocalVariablesAsync discovery pass to capture the EXACT variable names before binding — do not assume the dot->slash shorthand equals the Figma variable name (this file prefixes all with var/). Cache the name->VariableID map per fileKey+version.

trigger: fds-collapsible on-alternate-surface Stroke=Hidden variants (78071/78080) carried a borderColor TS token while the on-surface Hidden equivalents had none — cross-theme copy-paste artifact.
lesson: When auditing multi-theme variant sets, diff the token keys of Hidden/no-stroke variants across themes; a borderColor present on one theme but absent on the matching variant of another theme is a copy-paste artifact — strip it rather than binding NV to it.

trigger: SAGA subagent could not download Figma MCP asset URLs (no terminal tool in its context) and hand-authored approximate SVGs; ODIN later curled the real assets.
lesson: When dispatching SAGA as a subagent, ODIN should download the Figma MCP asset SVG/PNG URLs (from get_design_context) via terminal and place them in the component assets/ folder BEFORE or right after SAGA writes markup — subagents may lack a terminal to fetch remote assets. Keep SAGA filenames stable so refs survive the swap.

trigger: Sort.Overlay audit: effectStyleId was present on all COMPONENT nodes (TS boxShadow key matched), but the standard audit-resolve-digest.figma.js does not capture effectStyleId — it only captures fillStyleId. A supplemental elevation probe was required.
lesson: effectStyleId is not captured by audit-resolve-digest.figma.js (only fillStyleId is). For components with drop-shadow/elevation, always run a supplemental getStyleByIdAsync probe. In Figma there are 0 NV variables for effects — elevation is managed via effectStyleId only, not boundVariables. Reporting effectStyleId present = elevation IS bound natively.

trigger: Figma MCP asset export for the check icon arrived with preserveAspectRatio="none" + width/height=100%, which stretches a non-square icon (viewBox 0 0 11.7267 8.94).
lesson: Figma MCP icon/SVG exports often carry preserveAspectRatio="none" and width/height=100%. Before placing in assets/, rewrite to the intrinsic viewBox with preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" and explicit intrinsic width/height; render in a fixed-aspect box (object-fit:contain) so the icon is never stretched.

trigger: FDS-Badge Status type: TS fill uses var.fds.fds-*-shade tokens (type: color, linear-gradient) which bind via fillStyleId (paint style), NOT fills NV variable. NV fills array contains the two ref/system/*50+*60 gradient stops.
lesson: fds-*-shade tokens are linear-gradient color tokens; in Figma they create a paint style assigned via fillStyleId (not boundVariables.fills). hasFillNV() correctly returns true due to fillStyleId presence. The two-entry NV fills array (ref/system/*60 + ref/system/*50) are the gradient stops. No issue — this is the correct binding path for gradient fills.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add fds-success-shade, fds-info-shade, fds-alert-shade, fds-error-shade to Color section as type:color linear-gradient tokens (gradient paint styles, not NV variables)

trigger: FDS-Badge Content Type=Blank variants: all TS+NV tokens present (same 8 TS keys, same 14 NV props as other content types), zero children.
lesson: For FDS-Badge, Blank content type variants are dot indicators with full structural token coverage but empty children[] — they share the same token schema as Numerical/Text variants. Do not flag missing typography/fill tokens on Blank variants.

trigger: FDS-Badge Sportsbook/Bet status/Won: fill NV = var/fds/fds-sb-state-won but text fill NV = var/fds/fds-sb-on-state-win (win vs won suffix mismatch).
lesson: In this Figma file, the Sportsbook Bet status Won NV variable pair has asymmetric naming: fds-sb-state-won (fill) vs fds-sb-on-state-win (on-fill). This is an established variable name — do not attempt to rename during token writes, but flag for designer review when Sportsbook tokens are audited.

trigger: FDS-Badge audit: fds-*-shade tokens (success/info/alert/error) are gradient paint styles bound via fillStyleId (dual ref/system/*50+*60 NV stops), not a single fills NV; also absent from token-registry.md though present in ts-core-fabric.json.
lesson: fds-*-shade status tokens are linear-gradient paint styles bound via fillStyleId, not a scalar fills NV — hasFillNV via fillStyleId is correct, do not flag as MISSING_NV_FILL. Add fds-success-shade/info-shade/alert-shade/error-shade to token-registry.md.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add 4 gradient status tokens: fds-success-shade, fds-info-shade, fds-alert-shade, fds-error-shade (gradient paint styles, bound via fillStyleId, stops ref/system/<status>/50+60)

trigger: FDS-Badge Blank content-type variants have empty children[] but carry the full 8 TS keys + 14 NV props.
lesson: Blank content-type variants are fully tokenized (same container tokens as Numerical/Text, empty children[]). Do not flag them as missing typography/text bindings.

trigger: FDS-Badge SB/Bet status/Won: fill NV var/fds/fds-sb-state-won but text NV var/fds/fds-sb-on-state-win (won vs win).
lesson: Sportsbook Won variant has a won/win NV naming asymmetry (fds-sb-state-won vs fds-sb-on-state-win). Not a binding error — do not rename during writes; flag for designer review.

trigger: FDS-Input audit: floating Label TEXT node has fill_ts=fds-on-surface-m but fill_nv=fds-on-surface-hi across all non-focus Surface states; in some states (Success/Alt) TS uses semantic state color fds-success on the label which is wrong.
lesson: For FDS-Input label text: TS fill says -m emphasis but NV is bound to -hi emphasis — systematic misalignment. Focus state aligns correctly (both hi). This is a known TS-NV drift on the floating label. Also: Never use semantic state tokens (fds-success/fds-error) as fill on label TEXT nodes — use the correct emphasis token.

trigger: FDS-Input tokens live on inner FRAME child named Input (depth 1), NOT on the COMPONENT root. Only itemSpacing is on the COMPONENT root. Matrix building from root node.ts gives all ∅.
lesson: For FDS-Input: COMPONENT root has only itemSpacing token. All fill/border/padding/radius/strokeWeight tokens are on the child FRAME named Input (depth 1). Use depth >= 2 or target named-child probes when auditing — root-level matrix will show all ∅ for fill/border.

trigger: FDS-Input readonly state: strokeWeight NV is bound (fds-stroke-150) but no borderColor TS key or strokes NV binding — border width set, border color unbound.
lesson: FDS-Input readonly: borderColor is intentionally absent (readonly has no visible border emphasis color — renders with transparent or default stroke). Verify with designer whether readonly should show fds-on-surface-ulow border or none.

trigger: FDS-Input COMPONENT root holds only itemSpacing; all fill/border/padding/radius/strokeWeight tokens live on child FRAME Input (depth 1). Root-level audit shows false-empty for fills/border.
lesson: For FDS-Input (and nested input-like components), audit the inner FRAME named Input at depth>=1 — the COMPONENT root only carries itemSpacing. Root-only token reads give false MISSING_* results.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add note: FDS-Input nests structural tokens on child FRAME Input (depth 1); root carries only itemSpacing. Probe inner frames by name.

trigger: FDS-Input floating Label TEXT: TS fill = fds-on-surface-m (or alt -m) but NV bound to fds-on-surface-hi (or alt -hi) on ALL non-focus variants; only Focus aligns both at hi. Success/Alt-Surf-Var label uses fds-success TS key (wrong category).
lesson: FDS-Input floating Label has systematic TS/NV emphasis drift (TS -m vs NV -hi) on every non-focus variant. Never use semantic state tokens (fds-success/fds-error) as label TEXT fill — use text-emphasis tokens. Flag as TS_NV_CONFLICT, do not auto-rebind.

trigger: FDS-Input readonly state: strokeWeight (fds-stroke-150) bound TS+NV but NO borderColor TS key and NO strokes NV — border drawn with weight but no color token.
lesson: FDS-Input readonly variants bind strokeWeight but have no borderColor token (TS or NV). Confirm with designer whether readonly border should bind fds-on-surface-ulow or render transparent before any write.

trigger: FDS-Input Default-Error COMPONENT root carries a stale borderColor:fds-error TS key with baked rawStrokes rgb(249,85,77); the live binding is on inner FRAME Input.
lesson: Watch for stale borderColor TS + rawStrokes on the COMPONENT root of Default-Error inputs — a copy-paste artifact on the wrong layer. The real binding is on FRAME Input; strip the root copy rather than binding it.

trigger: fds-collapsible chevron icon: on-surface uses fds-on-surface-m (medium emphasis) but on-alternate-surface uses fds-on-alternate-surface-low (low emphasis). Emphasis levels differ across themes for the same UI element.
lesson: For fds-collapsible chevron: on-surface=-m, on-alternate-surface=-low. This emphasis asymmetry should be flagged for designer review — if intentional (different visual weight on alternate surface) document it; if accidental, align to same emphasis level (-m or -low consistently).

trigger: fds-collapsible audit: all 8 COMPONENT roots have correct TS+NV fill/border, but chevron icon VECTORs (4), title TEXT nodes (2), and content-slot INSTANCEs (2) have TS only — zero NV bindings on any inner layer node.
lesson: For fds-collapsible: COMPONENT root tokens (fill, borderColor) are TS+NV complete. Inner nodes (chevron VECTORs, title TEXTs, content-slot INSTANCEs) are TS-only — NV binding pass required. Also: the on-alternate-surface Stroke=Hidden Accordion-State=Open content slot (8889:78084) carries fds-surface-variant fill TS instead of fds-alternate-surface-variant — copy-paste artifact. Fix before NV write pass.

ruleProposal.diff: # fds-collapsible inner nodes need NV write pass: chevron VECTORs (fds-on-surface-m / fds-on-alternate-surface-low), title TEXT (fds-on-surface-hi / fds-on-alternate-surface-hi + Paragraphs.fds typography), content slots (fds-surface-variant / fds-alternate-surface-variant). Fix 8889:78084 wrong fill token first.

trigger: Phase 3 bulk write dispatched to MIMR subagent — mcp_figma_use_figma write tool not available in VS Code Copilot subagent context; only read tools (get_design_context, get_metadata, get_variable_defs) are present. PAT also expired, blocking REST fallback.
lesson: mcp_figma_use_figma (Plugin API execution) is only available in the ODIN main session context, not in MIMR/VALI/SAGA subagent contexts. Phase 3 writes must be executed from ODIN directly (inject script + call mcp_figma_use_figma there), or the user must run the script manually in Figma. If dispatching Phase 3 as a subagent, include the write-tool invocation in ODIN before dispatching — do not dispatch the write execution itself.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add note to Phase 3 step 3: mcp_figma_use_figma is ODIN-only. For subagent dispatch of Phase 3, ODIN should run the Plugin API call itself using the script built by MIMR.

trigger: Figma MCP in current VS Code session has no use_figma/plugin-exec tool — cannot write tokens directly. REST API returns null for freshly-created test nodes.
lesson: When mcp_figma_use_figma is unavailable (read-only MCP), generate Phase 3 script via generate-phase3.mjs and instruct user to paste in Figma Plugin console. Also: REST API may return null for nodes created in the same session — rely on MCP get_design_context which connects to live desktop app.

trigger: Attempted GET /v1/files/{key}/variables/local on mavdkFAsPZZiatzwZ39wsn — returned 403: requires file_variables:read scope which is not on the project PAT.
lesson: The project PAT for mavdkFAsPZZiatzwZ39wsn does not include file_variables:read scope. NV variable naming cannot be confirmed via REST API. Fall back to: (1) derive var names from TS dot-path (dot→slash) convention, (2) use generate-phase3.mjs findVar() suffix-match as safety net, (3) note this gap for ODIN to re-verify via Plugin API getLocalVariablesAsync on first script execution.

ruleProposal.diff: # Note: PAT for mavdkFAsPZZiatzwZ39wsn lacks file_variables:read; NV name discovery requires Plugin API (getLocalVariablesAsync) not REST. Derive names from TS dot→slash conversion and rely on findVar() suffix match.

trigger: Phase3 script wrote node.setBoundVariable('fills',0,v) directly and used getLocalVariablesAsync() for an externally-linked NV library ([Lib]: FDS Design Tokens) -> 0 local vars found, then 95/95 binds threw 'must be set on paints directly'.
lesson: When the NV library is a TEAM LIBRARY (not local to the file): (1) getLocalVariablesAsync() returns empty for library-only vars -- use figma.teamLibrary.getAvailableLibraryVariableCollectionsAsync() to find the collection, figma.teamLibrary.getVariablesInLibraryCollectionAsync(key) to resolve name->key, then figma.variables.importVariableByKeyAsync(key) per variable before binding. (2) For fills/strokes, never call node.setBoundVariable('fills',...) directly -- use figma.variables.setBoundVariableForPaint(paint, 'color', variable) on a cloned paint object, then reassign node.fills = [newPaint]. (3) Gradient (GRADIENT_LINEAR etc.) paints cannot take a solid color variable bind -- setBoundVariableForPaint throws 'can only bind variables to solid paints'; skip these as legitimate audit false-positives, do not force a fallback solid paint.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add: before Phase 3 bulk-update, detect library-linked NV collections (teamLibrary API) and prefer importVariableByKeyAsync over getLocalVariablesAsync; use setBoundVariableForPaint for fills/strokes.

trigger: Casino Lobby (1:16968) is a plain FRAME whose direct children are all INSTANCEs. Both audit-resolve-digest.figma.js and audit.figma.js have an INSTANCE guard that stops recursion at instance boundaries — running either script on this root yields only top-level FRAME bindings + instance count, zero audit coverage of the actual component content.
lesson: For FRAME roots whose children are placed INSTANCEs (not a COMPONENT_SET), the standard audit scripts cannot audit instance internals. The correct approach is: (1) use get_design_context or a targeted Plugin API call to get mainComponent.id for each instance, then (2) run audit-resolve-digest.figma.js on each mainComponent separately, OR (3) escalate to Opus and use a custom instance-recursive walk. Add audit-instances.figma.js as a new script to handle this pattern.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add note: for FRAME containers of placed instances, do NOT run audit-resolve-digest on the frame root — instead identify mainComponent.id for each instance and audit each component definition separately.

trigger: Casino Lobby audit prep: all gaming.* color tokens in token-index.json have empty NV column (fds-gaming-ribbon-*, fds-gaming-thumbnail-*, gaming.live.fds-gaming-live-*). Either TS-only by design, or NV names exist in team library but are not registered in token-registry.md.
lesson: Gaming-category tokens (gaming.fds-gaming-ribbon-*, gaming.fds-gaming-thumbnail-*, gaming.live.fds-gaming-live-*) have no NV short names in token-registry.md. Do not auto-generate NV write plan entries for these tokens without first running a getVariableByKeyAsync lookup against the FDS Design Tokens team library (key 66ad3b0aae1fc6eaf0081f6af41af1d609b53150) to confirm they exist. If not in library, flag as TS-only by design.

trigger: Figma REST /nodes endpoint returns empty children[] for COMPONENT_SET nodes regardless of depth param. The correct strategy for files where Plugin API is unavailable: traverse the CANVAS frame (placed instances) at depth=6 with plugin_data=shared — returns all 222 override nodes including TS sharedPluginData. Canvas IDs (I... format) are the correct write targets.
lesson: When Plugin API is unavailable, audit via REST canvas-traverse: GET /files/{key}/nodes?ids={canvasFrameId}&depth=6&plugin_data=shared. COMPONENT_SET REST endpoints (/components, /component_sets) return 0 results for unpublished components. Canvas instance override node IDs (I{placed};{main};{child}) are the write-plan targets. Start from the top-level placed frame, not from COMPONENT_SET roots.

ruleProposal.diff: # Note: For files without Plugin API access, use REST canvas-traverse (depth=6) from the placed frame. COMPONENT_SET /nodes returns empty children. Override node IDs are I{instance};{main};... format.

trigger: Casino Lobby MIMR audit: 0 gaming.* tokens found on canvas. All 21 gaming.* tokens in token-registry.md have empty NV columns. Team Library collection 66ad3b0aae1fc6eaf0081f6af41af1d609b53150 could not be verified via REST (no Plugin API). Registry evidence conclusive.
lesson: DISCARDED 2026-08-17: contradicted by live evidence — gaming.* tokens (e.g. gaming/fds-gaming-ribbon-new) DO resolve via the Core Brands/FDS Design Tokens team library and were successfully bound. Original claim (no NV equivalents) was based on REST-only audit without Plugin API/team-library access.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add note to gaming section: all gaming.* tokens are TS-only (no NV variable equivalents). Do not flag as MISSING_NV_FILL.

trigger: MIMR audited Casino Lobby via REST (no Plugin API in subagent context). 12/78 write-plan nodeIds failed 'not found' when ODIN executed via Plugin API: (1) entire HEADER hidden 'Mobile Bottom Drawer' subtree (7 tuples) -- REST metadata shows it as a child, but live Plugin document's header instance has only 1 child (visible 'Mobile Top Header'); (2) 5 carousel icon/heading nodes had a REST-reported override id (e.g. 11476:253646) that does not exist in the live Plugin tree -- the real sibling id differs (e.g. 11476:253981).
lesson: REST-based audits (used when Plugin API is unavailable to the MIMR subagent) can diverge from the live Plugin API document for: (a) hidden/inactive nested instance content that may have been detached or differs by document version, (b) instance-override child IDs on deeply nested instances, which occasionally differ between the REST snapshot and the live desktop session. Before executing a REST-derived write plan, ODIN should spot-check a sample of deep override node IDs via getNodeByIdAsync (or better, re-run the write-plan node list through get_design_context/get_metadata live) and only treat REST-derived IDs as provisional. When a 'not found' cluster correlates with hidden nodes or one component, don't keep guessing -- fetch the live children list directly (node.children) and re-map.

ruleProposal.diff: # Add: when MIMR audits via REST fallback (no Plugin API access), flag write-plan node IDs as provisional; ODIN must spot-check via getNodeByIdAsync/children listing before Phase 3, especially for hidden nested instance content and deep override paths.

trigger: User required instances not to be skipped during TS->NV audit/write; stock audit-resolve-digest.figma.js treats INSTANCE nodes as opaque leaves and never expands them
lesson: When a task explicitly requires including instances, do NOT use audit-resolve-digest.figma.js (it short-circuits at type===INSTANCE). Instead walk node.children recursively through instances too (Plugin API exposes instance-internal nodes/children normally) and read/write directly on the instance-nested node ids (I<inst>;<node> format) — writes there become per-instance overrides.

ruleProposal.diff: Codified as scripts/scan-bind-live.figma.js INCLUDE_INSTANCES flag + § Fast bind (live) section.

trigger: getLocalVariablesAsync() returned 0 variables for a consumer file whose tokens are all published from a team library (Fig Vars / FDS Design Tokens)
lesson: Before assuming TS->NV bind candidates have no variable, check figma.teamLibrary.getAvailableLibraryVariableCollectionsAsync() + getVariablesInLibraryCollectionAsync() when getLocalVariablesAsync() is empty or comes up empty for expected names. Match TS dot-path converted to slash against library variable .name, then figma.variables.importVariableByKeyAsync(key) before binding.

ruleProposal.diff: Added § Fast bind (live) section + scripts/scan-bind-live.figma.js entry documenting local-var-first then teamLibrary/importVariableByKeyAsync fallback.

trigger: Sportsbook-lobby frame has 87 TS-only candidates using a second naming scheme (T-shirt spacing XS/S/M/L/XL/3XL, semantic Sportbook.*/Feedback.*/Overlay.*/Neutral.* names) that do not match any variable in the Core Brands/FDS Design Tokens library (608 vars checked, 0 hits)
lesson: Sportsbook components appear to use a distinct/older TS token vocabulary not migrated to native variables in this library. Before assuming these are simply unmapped, check for a Sportsbook-specific team library collection (not yet found among the 9 enumerated) or ask the user whether these need manual mapping.

trigger: Set fds-mini-header props Left Side=none/Right side=none/Center=logo directly; combo doesn't exist among the 42 defined variants so Figma silently fell back to the default (icon-icon/icon-icon/text) ignoring all requested props.
lesson: For fds-mini-header (and any large multi-axis component_set), first read componentPropertyDefinitions AND the actual list of variantProperties combos before calling setProperties - not every combination of documented variant options is a real variant. Valid logo-center combos found: Left=none+Right=icon+Center=logo, Left=icon+Right=none+Center=logo, etc.

trigger: FDS-Button-Control-Two rendered as a stacked pair of two buttons (a two-button group), not a single secondary/low-emphasis button - despite the plausible name.
lesson: FDS-Button-Control-Two is a 2-button control group component, not a single secondary button. For a single lower-emphasis CTA use FDS-Button-Control-One with Hierarchy=Tertiary instead.

trigger: FDS-Stepper.Step-Group component_set only exposes Theme/Style/Text/Direction variant props - no active-step or step-count property to drive a 4-step wizard indicator.
lesson: FDS-Stepper.Step-Group renders one generic step unit (checkmark + connector); it cannot represent a specific step N of M via variant props alone. For a true multi-step wizard indicator, either place N instances side by side or ask the design team for a stepper variant with a step-index property.

trigger: Set layoutSizingHorizontal:'FILL' in $fig.autoLayout(...) creation options for a node with no parent yet -> 'FILL can only be set on children of auto-layout frames'.
lesson: Never pass layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical:'FILL' in the initial $fig.autoLayout/instance/text creation options when the node isn't yet a child of an auto-layout parent (e.g. a wrapper being built standalone then appended later). Create the node first, append/insertChild it into its auto-layout parent, THEN set layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' via raw node property assignment.

trigger: Interleaving raw figma.* async calls (getNodeByIdAsync, importComponentSetByKeyAsync) BETWEEN $fig.autoLayout/$fig.instance calls inside the same loop iteration produced 'Invalid handle' errors on the later $fig call, even though the same $fig.instance call worked fine in isolation.
lesson: Structure use_figma scripts that mix $fig creation with raw node lookups as three strict passes: (1) pure raw discovery — collect all needed node ids/indices into plain data, no $fig calls; (2) pure $fig creation — call all $fig.autoLayout/$fig.instance/etc. back-to-back with no raw awaits in between, then a single await $fig.done(); (3) pure raw mutation — re-fetch nodes by id and reparent/mutate. Do not interleave raw awaits with $fig plan-creation calls in the same loop body.

trigger: FDS-Card's only child 'Card Content Slot' is an INSTANCE, not a true Figma SLOT node, so custom content cannot be appended into it while the card stays a live library instance.
lesson: To put custom content inside FDS-Card: instantiate it, then detachInstance() the outer card (keeps fill/radius/elevation/padding), remove the default 'Card Content Slot' placeholder child, then appendChild your real content directly into the now-plain FRAME. This breaks live library sync for the card wrapper only - inner appended components stay live. Flag this tradeoff to the user as an open issue.

trigger: New screens placed at an x position beyond the parent canvas frame's existing width rendered as a blank/collapsed sliver in .screenshot(), even though the node's own width/height were correct - because the parent canvas FRAME has clipsContent=true.
lesson: Before placing new screens side-by-side on an existing canvas/page frame, check the parent's width and clipsContent. If new screens would extend past the parent's current width, resize the parent frame first (node.resize(newWidth, height)) - otherwise .screenshot() on the new screen can render blank/clipped even though its own dimensions are correct.

trigger: FDS-Stepper's per-step Color (Success/Info/Grey) and separator Color needed setting individually to show real progress; the separator does not auto-follow step colors.
lesson: For FDS-Stepper: set each FDS-Stepper.Ico-Circle's Color via setProperties per step (Success=done/Info=current/Grey=upcoming), AND separately set each FDS-Stepper.separator's Color (success/surface) to match, or connector lines stay green regardless of actual progress. Recorded in component-compendium.md.

trigger: Assigning node.fills = [{type:'SOLID', color: $fig.getVar(key)}] via raw mutation in Pass C threw 'Required value missing at [0].color.r ... Unrecognized key(s): _type, id, resolvedType, variable' - a $fig.getVar() handle is not a plain resolved color and can't be used in raw node.fills assignment.
lesson: $fig.getVar(...) handles only work as values passed INTO $fig creation calls (e.g. $fig.text({fills:[{type:'SOLID', color: $fig.getVar(key)}]})) - never assign them to node.fills directly in raw Pass-C mutation code. Set variable-bound fills at $fig creation time instead; if a fill must be set on an already-existing raw node, import the real Variable via figma.variables.importVariableByKeyAsync and use figma.variables.setBoundVariableForPaint.

trigger: After a use_figma script threw an error (raw fills-binding bug) mid-Pass-C, a subsequent read showed the ENTIRE test_canvas (all 6 previously-built, previously-screenshotted screens) had been wiped to zero children - not just the script's own changes rolled back. Mechanism not fully understood.
lesson: An uncaught error in a use_figma script can apparently cause loss of content well beyond that script's own changes, not just a clean rollback of the failing script. Treat any prior Figma state as NOT safely persisted until re-verified with a fresh get_metadata/screenshot after any script error - do not assume only the failing script's edits were affected. Flag data loss to the user immediately and suggest Figma version history for recovery rather than silently rebuilding from memory.

trigger: scan-bind-live.figma.js had no path for TS 'typography' tokens - they don't map to a bound variable, they map to node.textStyleId on a Figma TEXT STYLE, and there is no Plugin API 'get style by name' (unlike variables which have teamLibrary.getAvailableLibraryVariableCollectionsAsync).
lesson: Added a typography pass to scan-bind-live.figma.js: already-bound check is node.textStyleId !== '' (not boundVariables); dry run reports typography.distinctPaths (small list even when candidateTotal is large, since the same ramp step repeats across nodes); agent resolves each distinct TS dot-path's style key via search_design_system (includeStyles only, scoped to the FDS text-style library key) and injects TYPOGRAPHY_KEY_MAP; write pass imports each style once (cached) and sets node.textStyleId. Resolved keys get written back into token-index.json/token-registry.md 4th column, which for typography rows holds the style KEY (not an NV name) since styles have no name-lookup API.

trigger: User wanted default Figma layer names (Frame N) fixed inside a placed INSTANCE. The bad names lived 3-4 instance levels deep (root instance -> BX-Bonus Card instance -> FDS-Card instance -> local component instance), all read-only until detached. detachInstance() changes the node's id - the original ROOT_ID no longer resolves afterward.
lesson: To fix layer names buried inside nested instances: (1) confirm scope with the user first (which levels to detach, which cards/instances to include - detaching a shared library component like FDS-Card permanently breaks its link, always flag this explicitly); (2) detach each ancestor level in order (outermost first) via node.detachInstance(), capturing the returned/new node references directly rather than relying on the original id; (3) BEFORE renaming, apply VALI's single-child-no-pad-no-fill ungroup rule recursively (collapse whole chains, not just one level) - this eliminates most default-named wrapper frames entirely rather than just relabeling them; (4) only classify+rename what survives collapsing; (5) after detach, the root's old id is dead - relocate it via figma.currentPage.findAll(name match) if needed for a final screenshot.

trigger: User feedback: the manual detach+collapse+rename flow for fixing default layer names (189:18214, Bonus card list) took 11:34 min - too slow vs. MIMR's ~2 min scan-bind-live.figma.js fast path for TS->NV binding.
lesson: Built scripts/fix-names-live.figma.js: a deterministic two-call (DRY_RUN/write) script mirroring scan-bind-live.figma.js's pattern. Dry run does a fully read-only mirror-walk (descending through INSTANCE boundaries for reading only) to find every default-Figma-named node and collapse-candidate wrapper, computing the MINIMAL set of INSTANCE ancestors that actually need detaching (sibling instances with nothing wrong underneath are left alone, e.g. a real FDS-Badge). Write pass detaches only that minimal set, collapses whole redundant wrapper chains in one loop (not one ungroup per level), then classifies+renames survivors via the same structural rules as layout-rules.md. Smoke-tested clean (0 renames needed) against the already-fixed Bonus card list. Target ~2 min end to end.
